title: Merge Sort
intuition: Divide the array in half, sort each half recursively, then merge the two sorted halves.
whyExists: Guarantees $O(n \log n)$ worst-case time complexity while maintaining stability (equal elements preserve relative order).
analogy: Sorting a massive deck of papers by splitting it among friends, each sorting their half, then cleanly interleaving the stacks.
coreIdea: A classic divide-and-conquer algorithm. The array is split at mid = (l + r) / 2 until single-element base cases are reached. The merge() function combines two sorted subarrays using two moving pointers into an auxiliary buffer, copying back in $O(n)$ time per level.

complexity.reason: Recursion tree has depth log2(n), and merging across each level takes linear O(n) work.

pitfalls: High space overhead: requires allocating an auxiliary array for the merge buffer.
Integer overflow when calculating midpoint: use l + (r - l) / 2 rather than (l + r) / 2.
Losing stability by using < instead of <= when comparing elements from left and right halves.
